chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about backbiting. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is that you say to your brother regarding his religion something he has not done, and affirm a matter upon him which Allah has veiled, for which no legal punishment (Hadd) has been established upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of backbiting (ghibah) according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes backbiting by specifying that it involves attributing a religious flaw or a privately concealed matter to a person, provided no fixed legal punishment (hadd) applies, thereby separating it from formal slander. This definition underscores the nuance in Shia jurisprudence where the act targets the dignity of the individual regarding their faith or hidden states, rather than merely factual inaccuracies. The hadith serves as a critical boundary marker for social conduct, emphasizing the sanctity of the believer's inner and outer religious life.
